text:
NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions, normalization and residual paths make replacing an internal item with padding different from deleting its influence. Item ID 0 is not necessarily a zero vector: verify the actual checkpoint and initialization. Even with a zero embedding, convolution biases and neighboring inputs can create nonzero activations; affine normalization can introduce offsets. Residual connections preserve incoming activations, so masking only the convolution branch cannot remove the position’s representation. Feature-wise LayerNorm does not directly mix time positions, but normalization spanning time would make padding affect other positions’ statistics. These are architectural implications, not measured findings for the supplied model. The [NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) documents the convolution, normalization and residual structure; [RecBole’s implementation](https://recbole.io/docs/v1.0.0/_modules/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/nextitnet.html) illustrates biased convolutions and feature-wise LayerNorm.

Recommended controls: run evaluation mode with identical candidates; freeze the original readout index and sequence width; replace selected historical positions without compacting or shifting. For left-padded nonempty histories, read the original final position, never nonzero-count minus one. Define lag zero as that final observed item and exclude it; perturb only originally nonpadding positions at positive lags. Compare ID-0 replacement, explicit zero-embedding replacement, and valid-item substitution at matched positions and counts. Check a no-op intervention and interventions outside the causal receptive field; both should leave scores unchanged. Inspect padded-position activation norms through successive blocks. As a separate mechanistic control, clamp ablated positions after normalization/convolution and residual addition, recognizing that this changes computation. Report score/rank changes alongside validation HR changes. Agreement across substitutions supports history sensitivity; effects concentrated in zero-padding interventions suggest padding or out-of-distribution artifacts. Neither alone establishes causal temporal reliance.
